chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub and Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) about a man who had a female slave, who was then manumitted, married, and gave birth. Is it permissible for her first master to marry her daughter? He said, 'No, she is forbidden to him, and she is his daughter. The free woman and the slave are equal in this matter.'
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the daughter of the female slave he freed?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling of *al-ibahah* (marriage by manumission), establishing that a master who frees his female slave becomes her father-in-law, rendering her daughter forbidden to him. The narration explicitly equates the status of the freed slave (*umm walad*) with that of a free woman regarding marital prohibitions, a key principle in Shia fiqh for determining lineage and affinity.
